THE FRAMECHORD PLAYBOOK

## From an idea to *media.*

One command-line toolkit for the images, voices and sounds your project needs. Start with a brief. Preview the request. Make something worth reviewing.

[Explore use cases ↗](#scenarios) · [Get the examples ↓](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/tree/master/docs/site/examples)

Images · Infographics · Speech · Podcasts · Music · Sound effects

YOUR FIRST PREVIEW

```
# Describe the image. Pick the model.
framechord generate image \
  --provider google \
  --model gemini-nano-banana-2.1 \
  --prompt 'A tiny garden at sunrise' \
  --output garden.png \
  --dry-run --json
```

## See and hear it

A six-slide narrated tour, a one-minute podcast and an original music bed. Every image, voice and note in this section was generated by FrameChord from the job files linked below. Nothing here was edited by hand except for compression for the web.

1. <a id="slide-1"></a>![A terminal turning one brief into images, audio, music and infographics.](media/hero.jpg)

   ### What FrameChord is

   [Audio: slide-1-en.mp3](media/slide-1-en.mp3)

   FrameChord turns a written brief into finished media. It is one command-line tool for images, infographics, narration, podcasts, music and sound effects. It runs on your machine, keeps every input in plain YAML and Markdown files, and calls only the AI provider you choose. This narration was made with it, too.

2. <a id="slide-2"></a>![Infographic of the five steps: brief, validate, preview, generate, review.](media/info-workflow.jpg)

   ### One pattern for every medium

   [Audio: slide-2-en.mp3](media/slide-2-en.mp3)

   Every medium follows the same pattern. Write a brief. Validate it offline. Preview the exact request with a dry run, so nothing is billed yet. Generate only when the inputs are right. Then review the saved file before you use it.

3. <a id="slide-3"></a>![Infographic of defining, accepting and reusing a character.](media/info-characters.jpg)

   ### Define a character once

   [Audio: slide-3-en.mp3](media/slide-3-en.mp3)

   Characters are optional, but when you need one, you define it once. A character keeps its look and its voice in separate profiles, and its accepted references are reused in every new scene. Candidates never become canonical until a person accepts them.

4. <a id="slide-4"></a>![Infographic of parallel, isolated, cached and uncertain jobs.](media/info-recovery.jpg)

   ### Run together, recover safely

   [Audio: slide-4-en.mp3](media/slide-4-en.mp3)

   Independent jobs run together, within the limits you set. Each job keeps its own record, so one failure never erases another success. Identical requests reuse verified local results. And if a paid request ends in an uncertain state, FrameChord checks before paying for it twice.

5. <a id="slide-5"></a>![Infographic of a month of media costing about $2.20 at list prices.](media/info-cost.jpg)

   ### Pay per asset

   [Audio: slide-5-en.mp3](media/slide-5-en.mp3)

   There is no subscription and no FrameChord account. You pay each provider its API list price for what you generate. At October 2026 list prices, a month of forty illustrations, thirty minutes of narration, four music beds and twenty short sound effects comes to about two dollars and twenty cents.

6. <a id="slide-6"></a>![A terminal connected to several AI agents holding skill folders.](media/art-agents.jpg)

   ### Use it from any agent

   [Audio: slide-6-en.mp3](media/slide-6-en.mp3)

   FrameChord works with any agent that can run a process, including Claude Code and Codex. One command installs a project skill, so your agent can write the files, validate them and call the binary. The agent plans the work. FrameChord makes the media and keeps the receipts.

**Host:** Welcome to FrameChord in a minute. Here's the question every team asks: how do we make media without juggling five different apps?

AUDIOBOOK · TWO CHAPTERS

### The Lamp Counter

A short manuscript split at its headings, read by one Gemini voice, assembled into one MP3 with chapter markers.

[Audio: lamp-counter.mp3](media/audiobook/lamp-counter.mp3)

1. [Chapter One: The Platform](media/audiobook/chapter-01-chapter-one-the-platform.mp3) · 0:00
2. [Chapter Two: The Late Train](media/audiobook/chapter-02-chapter-two-the-late-train.mp3) · 0:30

**Text**

**Chapter One: The Platform**

The rain had stopped by the time Mara reached the station. She counted the lamps along the platform, the way her father had taught her: twelve on the near side, eleven on the far, because one had been broken for as long as she could remember.

Nobody else was waiting. The board said the last train was on time, which in this town meant nothing at all.

**Chapter Two: The Late Train**

The train arrived eleven minutes late, its windows fogged and gold. A conductor leaned out, looked at Mara, then at the broken lamp, and smiled as if the two of them shared a joke.

"Twelve and eleven," he said. "Still counting?"

She was. She stepped aboard, and behind her, for the first time in years, the twelfth lamp on the far side flickered on.

Google `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` · voice Charon · [job](media/jobs/audiobook.yaml) · [chapter index](media/audiobook/lamp-counter.chapters.json)

> **How this was made.** The audiobook sample was generated on October 19, 2026: two Gemini TTS requests, one per chapter, assembled and encoded locally. Generated on October 15, 2026 with FrameChord 0.7.0 in one batch of 33 jobs: OpenAI gpt-image-2.5-flare drew 9 illustrations and 4 infographics; Google gemini-3.8-flash-tts spoke 12 narrations and a 6-turn podcast; Google lyria-3.5 wrote the music. A rerun after raising a request limit reused 31 verified results from the local cache. One command ran every job in parallel: `framechord batch --manifest media/jobs/showcase-batch.yaml --limits-file media/jobs/limits.yaml`. Read the [batch manifest](media/jobs/showcase-batch.yaml) and the per-asset [provenance record](media/provenance.json). Successful generation is not proof of quality, so every image was inspected for exact text and stray lettering, and every narration passed a Google `gemini-3.8-flash` audio review against its script with `framechord review check --ai`. Estimated list price for the whole batch: about $0.37 for images and music, plus Gemini TTS, whose cost is unknown because only token totals were returned. <a id="delegate"></a>

ALREADY INSTALLED? DELEGATE IT

## Hand it to your agent

You do not need to learn every flag. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot or any agent that can run commands can drive FrameChord for you. Say what you want in plain words; the agent writes the brief files, previews the request for free and asks before anything is billed.

1. ### Install the skill in your project

   Run this once at the root of the repository where the media should live. It adds the FrameChord skill to `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, which every agent above discovers. Put your provider key in `.env` yourself; never paste keys into a chat.

   Terminal:

   ```
   cd my-project
   framechord init
   ```

2. ### Open your agent there and check readiness

   Start a new agent session in the same folder so it picks up the skill, then send this first prompt. It is free: nothing is generated.

   First prompt:

   ```
   Use the framechord skill. Check this project's FrameChord setup: run framechord config status and framechord doctor, tell me which providers and media types are ready, and what I still need to configure. Do not generate anything.
   ```

3. ### Ask for media in plain words

   Name your source files, where the results should go and anything that must stay exact. The agent follows the same loop every time:

   - **Author.** It writes a YAML job and a Markdown brief under `framechord/jobs/`, files you can read, edit and commit.
   - **Check.** It runs `framechord validate` and a `--dry-run`, which make no provider calls, and shows you the provider, model, settings and output paths it would use. A dry run does not price the request; ask the agent to compare it with the rates in [Pay per asset](#cost), and run `framechord usage` afterwards for labelled list-price estimates.
   - **Generate.** Only after you say go. This is the step your provider bills.
   - **Report.** It reviews the result and gives you the file paths and any job that failed or needs a decision.

> **Stay in charge.** The skill tells your agent to keep scripts, lyrics and figures exact, preview new inputs with a dry run, generate only when you asked for it, never retry an uncertain paid request without your say-so, and leave character references for you to choose. Provider, model and voice come from your saved configuration unless you ask for a change. Saying “preview first” and “generate only when I say go” makes your expectations explicit; set request limits for large batches.

### Prompt ideas by use case

Copy one, change the file names, and send it to your agent. Every prompt that can cost money asks for a preview and your go-ahead first.

<a id="case-prompt-cover"></a>

BLOG · IMAGES

### Illustrate a blog post

A cover image and one inline illustration that match the post, saved where your site expects them.

Prompt:

```
Read posts/launch.md. Use FrameChord to create a 16:9 cover image and one inline illustration that match the post. Write the briefs, validate them and show me the dry run. Generate only after I say go, save the images to public/images/launch/ and add them to the post.
```

<a id="case-prompt-narration"></a>

DOCS · NARRATION

### Listen to an article

One narration file read word for word, with a voice from your configured speech provider.

Prompt:

```
Use FrameChord to narrate docs/getting-started.md. Keep the wording exactly as written and skip code blocks. Use a calm, friendly voice from the configured speech provider. Preview the request first, then generate when I approve and tell me the output path.
```

<a id="case-prompt-podcast"></a>

A two-host script for your approval first, then the assembled audio.

Prompt:

```
Write a 90-second, two-host podcast script from the 2.3 section of CHANGELOG.md and show it to me before any audio is made. After I approve the script, author a FrameChord podcast job with two distinct voices, preview it, and generate it to media/release-2.3.mp3 when I say go.
```

<a id="made-by-agent"></a>

### Case study: how this guide got its media

Every picture, voice and note on this page came from one request to a coding agent with FrameChord installed. This was the request, lightly edited for grammar:

The original request:

```
Use FrameChord to improve the documentation of this project at docs/site/index.html with images, infographics and audio slides that explain the project and its benefits, and show it as a demo of the product. The API keys you need are in the .env file at the root of this repository.
```

From that one message, the agent:

1. Read the guide and planned the assets: a hero image, eight section illustrations, four infographics with exact text, a six-slide tour narrated in English and Spanish, a two-voice podcast and a music bed.
2. Wrote 27 job files and their briefs in [media/jobs/](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/tree/master/docs/site/media/jobs), plus one [batch manifest](media/jobs/showcase-batch.yaml) and a [limits file](media/jobs/limits.yaml).
3. Previewed the whole batch with `batch --dry-run`, which made no provider calls.
4. Ran the batch: 33 jobs in parallel. Three were held back by the request limit; after the limit was raised, the rerun reused 31 verified results from the local cache and paid only for the rest.
5. Checked every infographic label and number and had every narration reviewed against its script with `framechord review check --ai`.
6. Compressed the files for the web, placed them on this page and recorded hashes, models and usage in [provenance.json](media/provenance.json).

The estimated list price was about $0.37 for the images and music; speech cost is unknown because the provider returned only token totals. Read [the result](#showcase), then reuse the [same prompt](#case-prompt-docs) for your own site.

> **For agents reading this page.** A Markdown copy of the whole guide is at [index.md](index.md), and [llms.txt](llms.txt) lists it with install and usage notes. Point an agent at `https://framechord.com/llms.txt` to teach it FrameChord without a browser.

START WITH A REAL TASK

## What do you want to make?

Nine practical scenarios, from a single narrated article to a package of images and audio. Choose a task to see its inputs, deliverables, exact commands and review steps.

> New here? Complete [setup](#start) first. Every command below is an offline preview. Download the example pack into your project so `examples/` sits alongside `framechord/`. Generation is a separate, intentional step.

<a id="case-article-audio"></a>

SCENARIO 01

### Turn an article into audio

For a blog, newsletter or an audio version of a lesson.

**Start with:** A local article text file and a delivery brief.

**You get:** One narration WAV; long scripts also retain individual clips.

**Walk through this scenario**

1. **Prepare.** Download the embedded examples, extract them into your project and review the scenario files below.
2. **Preview.** Run these offline checks from the project root.

Preview command:

```
framechord generate speech \
  --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini-tts --voice alloy \
  --text-file examples/article.txt --brief-file examples/narration.md \
  --format wav --output outputs/article.wav --dry-run --json
```

**Open the scenario files**

article.txt:

```
A small garden can begin with a single pot. Choose a bright spot, check the soil before watering, and watch how the plant responds. A few minutes of attention each day can help you learn what it needs.
```

narration.md:

```
Read clearly, with a calm, warm delivery. Preserve every word of the supplied article.
```

**Generate.** When the effective inputs and limits are right, remove `--dry-run` from the generation or batch command. This can incur provider charges. Use returned artifact paths to locate results.

**Review.** Listen against the original: check every word, names, numbers and sentence endings. A saved WAV does not prove an accurate reading.

> The input must already be local text. Fetching a webpage, extracting the article and adapting its wording are separate tasks for your agent.

#### Give your agent the task

Scenario agent prompt:

```
Use FrameChord to narrate examples/article.txt exactly. Use the delivery notes in examples/narration.md. Preview OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts with alloy, show the output path and limits, then generate only when authorized. Report the final WAV, any chunks and pronunciation concerns.
```

[Open the detailed workflow →](#speech)

<a id="case-podcast-package"></a>

SCENARIO 02

### Produce a podcast episode package

For an interview-style explainer with an introduction and cover art.

**Start with:** Two exact speaker scripts, an image brief, a music brief and a batch manifest.

**You get:** An assembled episode WAV, the original speech clips, a cover PNG and a separate ten-second intro MP3.

**Walk through this scenario**

1. **Prepare.** Download the embedded examples, extract them into your project and review the scenario files below.
2. **Preview.** Run these offline checks from the project root.

Preview command:

```
framechord validate --kind batch examples/podcast-kit.yaml --json
framechord batch --manifest examples/podcast-kit.yaml \
  --limits-file examples/limits.yaml \
  --output-dir outputs/podcast-kit --dry-run --json
```

**Open the scenario files**

podcast-kit.yaml:

```
schema_version: 1
jobs:
  - image.yaml
  - podcast.yaml
  - music.yaml
```

podcast.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-podcast
media: podcast
brief: podcast.md
locale: en-US
turns:
  - id: host-intro
    text_file: host.txt
    selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-4o-mini-tts}
    settings: {voice: alloy, format: wav}
  - id: guest-answer
    text_file: guest.txt
    selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-4o-mini-tts}
    settings: {voice: nova, format: wav}
assembly:
  pause_ms: 250
  turn_gain_db: {host-intro: -1}
  loudness_lufs: -19
```

music.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-intro
media: music
selection: {provider: elevenlabs, model: music_v2_5}
brief: music.md
settings: {format: mp3, duration_seconds: 10, instrumental: true}
```

**Generate.** When the effective inputs and limits are right, remove `--dry-run` from the generation or batch command. This can incur provider charges. Use returned artifact paths to locate results.

**Review.** Check speaker order and distinct voices, all dialogue, joins and pauses, artwork framing and the music ending.

> The sample resolves four provider calls: one image, two speech turns and one music clip. The intro remains a separate file; mixing it under speech and publishing the episode are separate tasks.

#### Give your agent the task

Scenario agent prompt:

```
Produce a podcast asset package with FrameChord using examples/podcast-kit.yaml. Preview all four provider requests with examples/limits.yaml. Keep exact host/guest scripts and save outputs under outputs/podcast-kit. Report the assembled episode, source clips, artwork and separate intro music; do not claim the music has been mixed in.
```

[Open the detailed workflow →](#podcasts)

<a id="case-explain-data"></a>

SCENARIO 03

### Explain a schedule or set of numbers

For a poster, social graphic, project summary or presentation visual.

**Start with:** A structured infographic spec with exact copy, values, units and source notes, plus visual direction.

**You get:** One portrait PNG containing the requested information.

**Walk through this scenario**

1. **Prepare.** Download the embedded examples, extract them into your project and review the scenario files below.
2. **Preview.** Run these offline checks from the project root.

Preview command:

```
framechord validate --kind infographic examples/infographic.yaml --json
framechord generate --job examples/infographic-job.yaml \
  --output outputs/garden-schedule.png --dry-run --json
```

**Open the scenario files**

infographic-job.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-schedule
media: infographic
selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-image-2.5-flare}
spec: infographic.yaml
settings: {format: png, size: 1024x1536, image_quality: medium}
```

infographic.yaml:

```
schema_version: 1
title: "A little time for your garden"
audience: "New home gardeners"
key_message: "Make space for three short weekly sessions."
canvas: "1024x1536"
layout: "Title at top; three stacked cards; source note at bottom."
sections:
  - heading: "Monday"
    copy: "Check the soil and water if needed."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "5"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
  - heading: "Wednesday"
    copy: "Look for new leaves and check the light."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "5"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
  - heading: "Saturday"
    copy: "Tidy the pots and note what changed."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "10"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
visual_brief: infographic.md
references: []
```

infographic.md:

```
# Visual direction
Use a warm off-white background, dark green text, large readable headings and
three stacked cards. Add simple plant icons. Keep generous margins.
Render the title, copy, values, units and source note exactly as specified.
The schedule is an illustrative example, not measured research.
```

**Generate.** When the effective inputs and limits are right, remove `--dry-run` from the generation or batch command. This can incur provider charges. Use returned artifact paths to locate results.

**Review.** Compare every value, unit, heading and source note with the YAML at full image size. Incorrect data means the output needs revision.

> The 5 / 5 / 10 minute schedule is illustrative. FrameChord renders a raster image; it does not research facts or deliver an editable chart.

#### Give your agent the task

Scenario agent prompt:

```
Create a schedule infographic with FrameChord from examples/infographic-job.yaml. Keep Monday 5 minutes, Wednesday 5 minutes and Saturday 10 minutes exact. Preserve the illustrative source note. Preview before generation and compare the resulting text with the source spec.
```

<a id="case-lesson-package"></a>

SCENARIO 04

### Create a visual and audio lesson

For a short course unit that learners can look at or listen to.

**Start with:** An infographic specification and a separately authored narration covering the same points.

**You get:** A schedule PNG and a matching narrated WAV generated as independent jobs.

**Walk through this scenario**

1. **Prepare.** Download the embedded examples, extract them into your project and review the scenario files below.
2. **Preview.** Run these offline checks from the project root.

Preview command:

```
framechord validate --kind batch examples/lesson-kit.yaml --json
framechord batch --manifest examples/lesson-kit.yaml \
  --limits-file examples/limits.yaml \
  --output-dir outputs/lesson-kit --dry-run --json
```

```
Make time for three short garden check-ins each week. On Monday, spend five minutes checking the soil and watering if needed. On Wednesday, take five minutes to look for new leaves and check the light. On Saturday, spend ten minutes tidying the pots and noting what changed. For a novel, a course or a long report you want as an audiobook.
```

**Walk through this scenario**

Preview command:


**Open the scenario files**

audiobook.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: lamp-counter
media: audiobook
brief: audiobook-narration.md
manuscript: manuscript.md
split: {heading_level: 1}
locale: en-US
assembly:
  pause_ms: 1500
  loudness_lufs: -19
audiobook:
  output_mode: full
  format: mp3
  announce_titles: true
  title: The Lamp Counter
  author: FrameChord guide
```

manuscript.md:

```
---
title: The Lamp Counter
note: A two-chapter sample written for the FrameChord guide.
---

# Chapter One: The Platform

The rain had stopped by the time Mara reached the station. She counted the lamps along the platform, the way her father had taught her: twelve on the near side, eleven on the far, because one had been broken for as long as she could remember.

Nobody else was waiting. The board said the last train was on time, which in this town meant nothing at all.

# Chapter Two: The Late Train

The train arrived eleven minutes late, its windows fogged and gold. A conductor leaned out, looked at Mara, then at the broken lamp, and smiled as if the two of them shared a joke.

"Twelve and eleven," he said. "Still counting?"

She was. She stepped aboard, and behind her, for the first time in years, the twelfth lamp on the far side flickered on.
```

**Generate.** Remove `--dry-run` to make the first chapter, listen to it, then run the same command without `--chapter`. If the book exceeds your run limits, FrameChord stops before any request and names the limits to raise. This can incur provider charges.

**Review.** Listen for skipped or changed words, mispronounced names, the pause between chapters and the chapter markers in your player.

> The sample makes one speech request per chapter, two in total. Longer chapters are split at paragraph boundaries into requests of at most 4,000 characters.

#### Give your agent the task

Scenario agent prompt:

```

```

<a id="start"></a>

01 / SETUP

## Set up once. Finish at your pace.

A guided terminal checklist with arrow-key choices, search and clear readiness. Initialization stays offline.

[![Infographic: One pattern for every medium. 1 Brief, 2 Validate, 3 Preview with zero provider calls, 4 Generate, 5 Review. Nothing is billed until you choose Generate.](media/info-workflow.jpg)](media/info-workflow.jpg)

Infographic from an exact spec · Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/info-workflow-spec.yaml)

1. ### Install and start

   Install without Rust or administrator access. Public release downloads do not require GitHub sign-in.

   macOS / Linux:

   ```
   curl -fsSL https://framechord.com/install.sh | sh
   ```

   Windows PowerShell:

   ```
   irm https://framechord.com/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

   Already downloaded? Run `./framechord install` (Windows `./framechord.exe install`). It installs in your user bin directory, adds user PATH when needed, and keeps project files and skills untouched. Use `--no-modify-path` to preserve profiles. Open a new terminal, then initialize your project. See [custom install options](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/blob/master/docs/INSTALLATION.md) or [manual release downloads](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/releases/latest).

   Check, update, or restore the preceding binary:

   ```
   framechord update --check
   framechord update
   framechord update --rollback
   ```

   Updates verify GitHub’s SHA-256 digest and executable version before replacement and keep one previous binary for offline rollback. Configuration, provider keys, characters, references, generated media and installed skills are preserved. Skill refresh and project initialization remain explicit. Supported release targets: macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64. Checksums are separate from code signing.

   From the source checkout, install with Cargo. Download native binaries directly from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/releases/latest). CI artifacts remain available for development builds. Binaries include the skills and templates.

   Terminal:

   ```
   cargo install --path . --locked
   framechord init ./my-project
   ```

2. ### Choose Recommended setup

   Init reads the chosen project’s `.env`, creates it when absent, and appends missing `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `FISH_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` entries with empty values. Existing values, comments and unrelated entries stay intact. Shell credentials take precedence and are never copied into the file. With no destination, this is the folder where you run the command; an explicit project owns its own `.env`. On save, both `.agents/skills/framechord/` and `.claude/skills/framechord/` are installed by default. Select fewer agents with `--agents codex` or `--agents claude`. Existing modified skills and character models are preserved.

   If this folder contains the downloaded executable named `framechord`, start with `./framechord init ./my-project`. Setup needs its own `framechord/` directory. Setup detects name conflicts before the checklist and offers a project folder; existing files stay untouched. When PATH is omitted, `--project` selects the destination, otherwise the current folder is used. An explicit `init PATH` takes precedence. The full destination appears before setup and during save review.

   Google is the default: Nano Banana 2.1 handles images and infographics; Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS uses built-in Kore for speech and podcasts; Lyria 3.5 handles music; Gemini 3.8 Flash handles planning. Set GEMINI_API_KEY to make these defaults locally ready. OpenAI is the second welcome option, or use --preset openai for images, speech with coral, and planning. Standalone effects remain optional with ElevenLabs. Providers never change automatically.

   Use arrows and Enter, type to search, and Escape to return. The wizard loops back to this checklist after every section:

   Setup checklist:

   ```
   Features and models
   API keys
   Voices
   Agent skills
   Characters (optional)
   Advanced settings
   Review and finish setup
   Save unfinished setup and exit
   Discard changes and exit
   ```

3. ### Reuse your key and review the voice

   An existing GEMINI_API_KEY is read automatically from the shell or this project’s .env. The default Google voice is Kore; the OpenAI alternative uses coral. Keep the built-in voice or change it in Voices. Missing keys can be entered without echo; values are written only when you save. No provider voices are created and setup makes no network calls.

   Review your choices before saving. Finish requires all enabled features to be locally ready. Save unfinished setup and run init again to resume. Existing configuration, character references and credentials are preserved unless explicitly changed.

4. ### Check readiness

   Terminal:

   ```
   framechord --project ./my-project config status --json
   framechord --project ./my-project config show --json
   ```

   Local readiness does not verify authentication, billing, account voice access or media quality. For an explicit read-only authentication check:

   Optional online check:

   ```
   framechord --project ./my-project doctor --live --provider google --json
   ```

**For agents: setup without menus**

JSON and noninteractive calls never prompt. Read setup_complete and pending_steps: successful scaffold creation can still leave incomplete setup. Use --preset empty for an empty scaffold, or --defaults-file for an exact custom configuration.

Agent commands:

```
framechord init ./my-project --preset recommended --json --non-interactive
framechord init ./openai-project --preset openai --json --non-interactive
framechord --project ./my-project config status --json
framechord --project ./my-project config setup --file my-config.yaml --json
```

**Current stable models and explicit discovery**

Only current, reviewed stable model families may submit new provider requests. Older and preview models are unavailable for new generation, planning, reviews and retries. Historical files, receipts and successful results remain readable. A pinned older character needs a new character version with newly accepted references; never change its origin metadata to bypass its model lock.

Model selection:

```
framechord models --media image --recommended
framechord models --provider fish --media speech
framechord models --all --search image
framechord models --live --provider openrouter --media image --sort popular --json
```

The bundled catalog was verified on October 14, 2026. It is an offline snapshot, not account entitlement or a promise of knowledge about future releases. Explicit live discovery caches a bounded provider listing; it never enables unimplemented models. Popularity, where shown, is provider-reported OpenRouter usage. Initialization never refreshes catalogs. Current GPT Image 2.5 models omit input_fidelity.

<a id="cost"></a>

02 / COST

## Pay per asset, not per month

FrameChord has no subscription, credits or account. Each request is billed by the provider you configured at its API list price; keys, inputs and receipts stay in your repository.

[![Infographic: Pay per asset, not per month. About $2.20 for a month of media: 40 illustrations $1.34, 30 minutes of narration $0.41, 4 music beds $0.32, 20 sound effects $0.12. Official API list prices read October 15, 2026.](media/info-cost.jpg)](media/info-cost.jpg)

Infographic from an exact spec · Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/info-cost-spec.yaml)

**Official list prices, read on October 15, 2026**

| Asset | Default model | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image or infographic | Google Nano Banana 2.1 | $0.0336 per 1K image; $0.0504 at 2K; $0.113 at 4K |
| Narration or podcast turn | Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS | $9.00 per 1M audio tokens, stated by Google as $0.00225 per 10 seconds of audio through 2026 |
| Music bed or song | Lyria 3.5 | $0.08 per song |
| Sound effect | ElevenLabs eleven_text_to_sound_v2 | $0.12 per minute |
| Narration alternative | ElevenLabs eleven_flash_v2_5 / eleven_v3 | $0.04 / $0.08 per 1,000 characters |

A month of 40 illustrations, 30 minutes of narration, 4 music beds and 20 three-second effects costs about $2.20 at these rates ($1.34 + $0.41 + $0.32 + $0.12), and between $2 and $4 with any ElevenLabs variant. Higgsfield Starter is $19 a month for about 100 image generations; Magnific Premium is $20 a month for 240,000 credits a year, of which that month uses about 3,940. Both are roughly nine times the provider price at this volume.

> **When a plan is the better choice:** video (FrameChord makes none), upscaling, several hundred images a month through one model, or a visual editor and gallery. At full use Magnific's bundled Nano Banana 2 price, about $0.075 per 2K image, beats that older model's list price; the current Nano Banana 2.1 is $0.0504 at 2K.

Labelled estimates beside provider-reported units:

```
framechord usage --json
framechord usage --price-table my-rates.yaml --json
```

Each job reports `cost_status` as estimated, provider_reported, cached_no_charge or not_estimable, with the price table's verification date; `currency_total` stays null because unknown is not zero. Rates, sources, the worked month and a refresh checklist are in [docs/COST.md](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/blob/master/docs/COST.md).

<a id="integrate"></a>

03 / YOUR PROJECT

## Use it in your own project

Initialize inside an existing repository, commit the authored files, and call the binary from any script or agent.

Terminal:

```
cd my-app
framechord init
framechord init ./apps/site --preset recommended --json --non-interactive
```

**What init creates**

| Path | Commit it? |
| --- | --- |
| `framechord/config.yaml`, `templates/`, `characters/`, `jobs/` | Yes |
| `framechord/runs/`, `cache/`, `blobs/`, `setup.lock` | No; init appends these rules to the root `.gitignore` and leaves other lines alone |
| `.env` | No; missing key names are appended, existing values kept, file ignored |
| `.env.example`, `.agents/skills/framechord/`, `.claude/skills/framechord/` | Yes |

> The process environment takes precedence over `.env`; parent folders are never searched. Outputs named with `--output` go where you ask; everything else lands under the ignored `framechord/runs/`. `framechord/characters/*/character.lock` is not ignored automatically.

### From scripts and code

Results are a JSON envelope on stdout (`ok`, `data`, `errors`, `warnings`); progress stays on stderr. Exit codes: 0 success or accepted, 1 internal, 2 invalid input, 3 provider or local failure, 4 partial batch, 5 needs revision, 6 limit reached, 7 outcome unknown, 130 interrupted wait. Preview with `--dry-run` first.

Python:

```
import json, subprocess

def framechord(*arguments, project="."):
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["framechord", "--project", project, "--json", "--non-interactive", *arguments],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    return result.returncode, json.loads(result.stdout)  # stderr holds progress

code, response = framechord("generate", "speech", "--text-file", "article.txt",
                            "--output", "narration.wav")
if code == 0:
    paths = [a["path"] for job in response["data"]["jobs"] for a in job["artifacts"]]
elif code == 7:
    raise RuntimeError("outcome unknown; reconcile before any retry")
```

Shell with jq:

```
framechord --project . generate image \
  --prompt 'A teal leaf on a cream background' --output assets/leaf.png \
  --json --non-interactive > result.json
status=$?
jq -r '.data.jobs[].artifacts[].path' result.json
test "$status" -eq 0 || jq -r '.errors[].message' result.json >&2
```

### Other coding agents

**Skill discovery, verified October 15, 2026**

| Agent | Project directories it reads | `--agents` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `.agents/skills/` | `codex` (default) |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/` | `claude` (default) |
| Cursor | `.cursor/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` | `cursor` |
| Gemini CLI | `.gemini/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` | `gemini` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` | `opencode` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` | `copilot` |

The default install is already discovered by Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot. Use `--agents cursor,copilot` for native directories, `--agents none` for no skill, and `skills export DIRECTORY` plus a pointer in your `AGENTS.md` for any other agent. The full guide, with gitignore details, a Node example and user-scope paths, is [docs/INTEGRATION.md](https://github.com/maxiplux/framechord/blob/master/docs/INTEGRATION.md).

<a id="basics"></a>

04 / THE COMMAND CONTRACT

## One pattern, every medium

Tell the CLI what to create, what to read, which model to use, and where the result belongs.

Command pattern — replace the uppercase placeholders:

```
framechord generate MEDIA \
  --provider PROVIDER --model MODEL \
  --brief-file examples/brief.md \
  --output outputs/result.ext \
  --dry-run --json
```

**Choose the right input**

| Option | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `--prompt / --brief-file` | Creative direction. Use one, not both. |
| `--text / --text-file` | Exact speech. A prompt is not a narration script. |
| `--spec` | Structured infographic copy, numbers, units and layout. |
| `--job` | A reusable YAML request, including podcast turns or a cast. |
| `--output` | One final filename. Use `--output-dir` for a batch or podcast clips. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and inspect effective inputs; no provider calls or run creation. |
| `--json --non-interactive` | Structured stdout for agents; progress and diagnostics go to stderr. |

> Generation examples below are previews. **Remove `--dry-run` to generate**, after reviewing inputs and limits. Those calls can incur provider charges. Completed results include artifact paths and a durable run ID. Existing output files require explicit `--overwrite`.

<a id="images"></a>

05 / IMAGE

## An image for an article

Create a cover, illustration or standalone visual from a specific creative brief.

![A sketched brief card turning into a framed finished illustration, checked with a magnifier.](media/art-images.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-images.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord generate image \
  --provider openai --model gpt-image-2.5-flare \
  --brief-file examples/image.md \
  --size 1536x1024 --image-quality medium --format png \
  --output outputs/garden-cover.png --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · image.md**

image.md:

```
# Article cover
Purpose: a calm editorial illustration about urban gardening.
Subject: three terracotta pots with leafy herbs on a sunny balcony.
Composition: wide view with empty space on the left for a separately added title.
Style: soft paper texture, forest green and warm cream. No lettering or logos.
```

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Use FrameChord to create an editorial image for an urban gardening article. Read examples/image.md, keep the left side clear for a title, and save to outputs/garden-cover.png. Validate with --dry-run first and show me the resolved provider, model and limits before generation.
```

> Expected result: one PNG plus its recorded inputs and provenance. Inspect composition and unwanted text before using it. Reference roles are distinct: use `--identity-reference` for a selected character, not a generic `--reference`.

<a id="infographics"></a>

06 / INFOGRAPHIC

## Make the facts part of the input

An infographic needs an exact content specification as well as visual direction. Keep copy and numeric strings in YAML.

Every infographic on this page was rendered from a spec like the one below: exact title, copy and values in YAML, visual direction in Markdown. Raster text still gets a human check.

- [![Infographic: One pattern for every medium. 1 Brief, 2 Validate, 3 Preview with zero provider calls, 4 Generate, 5 Review. Nothing is billed until you choose Generate.](media/info-workflow.jpg)](media/info-workflow.jpg)[spec](media/jobs/info-workflow-spec.yaml) → output
- [![Infographic: Pay per asset, not per month. About $2.20 for a month of media: 40 illustrations $1.34, 30 minutes of narration $0.41, 4 music beds $0.32, 20 sound effects $0.12. Official API list prices read October 15, 2026.](media/info-cost.jpg)](media/info-cost.jpg)[spec](media/jobs/info-cost-spec.yaml) → output
- [![Infographic: Define a character once. 1 Define, 2 Accept, 3 Reuse. Pose, outfit and mood are per-job direction; a new model needs a new character version.](media/info-characters.jpg)](media/info-characters.jpg)[spec](media/jobs/info-characters-spec.yaml) → output
- [![Infographic: Run together, recover safely. Parallel, isolated, cached, and uncertain paid requests are checked rather than resent.](media/info-recovery.jpg)](media/info-recovery.jpg)[spec](media/jobs/info-recovery-spec.yaml) → output

Terminal:

```
framechord validate --kind infographic examples/infographic.yaml --json
framechord generate infographic \
  --provider openai --model gpt-image-2.5-flare \
  --spec examples/infographic.yaml \
  --size 1024x1536 --image-quality medium --format png \
  --output outputs/garden-schedule.png --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · infographic.yaml, infographic.md**

infographic.yaml:

```
schema_version: 1
title: "A little time for your garden"
audience: "New home gardeners"
key_message: "Make space for three short weekly sessions."
canvas: "1024x1536"
layout: "Title at top; three stacked cards; source note at bottom."
sections:
  - heading: "Monday"
    copy: "Check the soil and water if needed."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "5"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
  - heading: "Wednesday"
    copy: "Look for new leaves and check the light."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "5"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
  - heading: "Saturday"
    copy: "Tidy the pots and note what changed."
    values:
      - label: "Time"
        value: "10"
        unit: "minutes"
        source: "Illustrative weekly schedule"
visual_brief: infographic.md
references: []
```

infographic.md:

```
# Visual direction
Use a warm off-white background, dark green text, large readable headings and
three stacked cards. Add simple plant icons. Keep generous margins.
Render the title, copy, values, units and source note exactly as specified.
The schedule is an illustrative example, not measured research.
```

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Use FrameChord to make an infographic from examples/infographic.yaml. Preserve Monday 5 minutes, Wednesday 5 minutes and Saturday 10 minutes exactly, including the illustrative source note. Preview first. After generation, compare every word and value with the YAML and report errors.
```

> Expected result: a raster PNG, not an editable chart. The compiler preserves exact source content in the request; the model may still render incorrect text. Check numbers, units, spelling, source notes, contrast and clipping at full size.

<a id="speech"></a>

07 / SPEECH

## Read an article aloud

Give the CLI the exact words to speak and a separate brief for delivery.

![A page of script lines curling into an audio waveform that flows into a studio microphone.](media/art-speech.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-speech.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord generate speech \
  --provider openai --model gpt-4o-mini-tts --voice alloy \
  --text-file examples/article.txt \
  --brief-file examples/narration.md --format wav \
  --output outputs/article.wav --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · article.txt, narration.md**

article.txt:

```
A small garden can begin with a single pot. Choose a bright spot, check the soil before watering, and watch how the plant responds. A few minutes of attention each day can help you learn what it needs.
```

narration.md:

```
Read clearly, with a calm, warm delivery. Preserve every word of the supplied article.
```

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Read examples/article.txt aloud with FrameChord using OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts and alloy. Preserve every word. Preview the request, save the final WAV to outputs/article.wav, and report chunk artifacts if the text is split.
```

> Use a local UTF-8 text file; this command does not fetch an article URL. Long supported scripts split at model limits and assemble locally into WAV while retaining source clips. Listen for omitted words, names and numbers.

<a id="podcasts"></a>

08 / PODCAST

## Give each speaker a turn

Author the conversation explicitly. Each turn has its own script, model and voice; the CLI generates clips and assembles the episode.

![Two studio microphones facing each other, their alternating waveforms merging into one track.](media/art-podcasts.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-podcasts.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord validate --kind job examples/podcast.yaml --json
framechord generate --job examples/podcast.yaml \
  --output-dir outputs/podcast \
  --limits-file examples/limits.yaml --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · podcast.yaml, host.txt, guest.txt, podcast.md**

podcast.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-podcast
media: podcast
brief: podcast.md
locale: en-US
turns:
  - id: host-intro
    text_file: host.txt
    selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-4o-mini-tts}
    settings: {voice: alloy, format: wav}
  - id: guest-answer
    text_file: guest.txt
    selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-4o-mini-tts}
    settings: {voice: nova, format: wav}
assembly:
  pause_ms: 250
  turn_gain_db: {host-intro: -1}
  loudness_lufs: -19
```

host.txt:

```
Welcome to Small Habits. Today we are talking about making room for a small garden. Where should we begin?
```

guest.txt:

```
Start with one pot and one plant. Choose a bright spot, and check the soil before watering.
```

podcast.md:

```
A friendly, concise conversation. Clear articulation and natural pauses. Speak only the exact text assigned to each turn.
```

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Build a two-speaker podcast with FrameChord using examples/podcast.yaml. Keep the host and guest scripts exact, preserve turn order, and use separate voices. Preview the two speech requests, then save the final WAV and original clips under outputs/podcast.
```

> This example makes two speech requests when executed. `pause_ms`, per-turn gain and optional EBU R128 loudness normalization apply to the local assembly. Original clips remain available. Converting an article into dialogue is an authoring step before generation.

<a id="audiobooks"></a>

09 / AUDIOBOOK

## Read a whole book aloud

One narrator reads your exact text, chapter by chapter. Get a file per chapter, or the whole book with chapter markers, from a Markdown manuscript or an explicit chapter list.

An audiobook is not a podcast. A podcast is a conversation between speakers; an audiobook keeps one voice and every word of the source. Put the book in one Markdown file with a `#` heading per chapter, or list chapter files in the job. [Hear a two-chapter sample](#sample-audiobook) made this way.

Terminal:

```
framechord validate --kind job examples/audiobook.yaml
# One chapter first, to check the voice
framechord generate --job examples/audiobook.yaml \
  --chapter chapter-one-the-platform \
  --output-dir outputs/audiobook --dry-run --json
# The whole book; finished chapters are reused from cache
framechord generate --job examples/audiobook.yaml \
  --output-dir outputs/audiobook --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · audiobook.yaml, manuscript.md, audiobook-narration.md, audiobook-chapters.yaml**

audiobook.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: lamp-counter
media: audiobook
brief: audiobook-narration.md
manuscript: manuscript.md
split: {heading_level: 1}
locale: en-US
assembly:
  pause_ms: 1500
  loudness_lufs: -19
audiobook:
  output_mode: full
  format: mp3
  announce_titles: true
  title: The Lamp Counter
  author: FrameChord guide
```

manuscript.md:

```
---
title: The Lamp Counter
note: A two-chapter sample written for the FrameChord guide.
---

# Chapter One: The Platform

The rain had stopped by the time Mara reached the station. She counted the lamps along the platform, the way her father had taught her: twelve on the near side, eleven on the far, because one had been broken for as long as she could remember.

Nobody else was waiting. The board said the last train was on time, which in this town meant nothing at all.

# Chapter Two: The Late Train

The train arrived eleven minutes late, its windows fogged and gold. A conductor leaned out, looked at Mara, then at the broken lamp, and smiled as if the two of them shared a joke.

"Twelve and eleven," he said. "Still counting?"

She was. She stepped aboard, and behind her, for the first time in years, the twelfth lamp on the far side flickered on.
```

audiobook-narration.md:

```
Read as an audiobook narrator: warm, unhurried and clear. Let each sentence finish and pause briefly at paragraph breaks. Give the conductor's single line a light, amused lift without a character voice.
```

audiobook-chapters.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: lamp-counter-chapters
media: audiobook
brief: audiobook-narration.md
chapters:
  - id: platform
    title: "Chapter One: The Platform"
    text_file: chapter-01.md
  - id: late-train
    title: "Chapter Two: The Late Train"
    text_file: chapter-02.md
locale: en-US
assembly: {loudness_lufs: -19}
audiobook:
  output_mode: chapters
  format: wav
  announce_titles: true
```

### How chapters are found

- Each `#` heading at or above `split.heading_level` starts a chapter. Headings inside code fences, `#tags` and indented or escaped `#` are ignored.
- YAML front matter between `---` lines is never read aloud. Text before the first heading becomes a `preamble` chapter unless you skip it.
- Heading lines are spoken only with `announce_titles: true`. Chapter IDs come from the titles, for example `chapter-one-the-platform`.
- `validate` prints every chapter with its source lines, length, request count and first and last words, and warns about links, tables or markup a voice might read out.

### What you get

- `outputs/audiobook/lamp-counter/chapter-01-chapter-one-the-platform.mp3` and one file per chapter (WAV or MP3).
- With `output_mode: full`: `lamp-counter.mp3` with ID3 chapter markers, `lamp-counter.chapters.json` with start times, durations and hashes, and a `lamp-counter.cue` sheet.
- With `output_mode: chapters`: chapter files and the chapter index only.

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Turn manuscript/my-novel.md into an audiobook with FrameChord, one chapter per # heading, read by a single warm narrator. Do not change any words. Validate it, show me the chapter list, the totals and whether it fits my limits, then generate chapter 1 only to audio/my-novel/ as MP3 so I can listen before the rest.
```

> A whole book is far larger than the default run limits (20 requests, 60,000 speech characters). FrameChord checks the entire book before the first request and, if it does not fit, stops without calling the provider and names the limits to raise. Raise them only when you mean to pay for the book, or generate a few chapters per run with `--chapter`. `revise --chapter ID` re-reads one chapter with new direction and reassembles the book. Audio is 24 kHz mono, which is not an ACX/Audible delivery spec; WAV books stop at about 24.8 hours. MP3 encoding uses the bundled LAME library under the LGPL (`framechord notices`).

<a id="music"></a>

10 / MUSIC

## A music bed or an original song

Describe mood, instrumentation, structure and duration. Choose instrumental or vocal explicitly.

![A brief card releasing layered sound waves around a keyboard, guitar and hand drum.](media/art-music.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-music.yaml)

### Instrumental podcast intro

Terminal:

```
framechord generate music \
  --provider elevenlabs --model music_v2_5 \
  --brief-file examples/music.md \
  --duration-seconds 10 --instrumental --format mp3 \
  --output outputs/intro.mp3 --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · music.md**

music.md:

```
# Podcast opening music
Purpose: a ten-second instrumental opening for a gardening podcast.
Mood: optimistic, relaxed and welcoming.
Instruments: soft acoustic guitar, light hand percussion and warm keys.
Structure: short opening motif, gentle development, clean ending.
No singing, spoken words, artist imitation or recognizable existing melody.
```

### Short vocal song

Terminal:

```
framechord generate music \
  --provider elevenlabs --model music_v2_5 \
  --brief-file examples/vocal.md \
  --duration-seconds 20 --vocal --format mp3 \
  --output outputs/song.mp3 --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · vocal.md**

vocal.md:

```
# Original short song
Mood: light, playful acoustic folk. One clear lead singer.
Duration: about twenty seconds; a short intro and a resolved ending.
Sing these original lyrics in this order:

One little seed, a patch of sun,
A quiet morning has begun.
Leaf by leaf, we watch it grow,
Small beginnings, nice and slow.

Do not add verses. Review the actual audio for omitted or changed lyrics.
```

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Use FrameChord for a ten-second instrumental podcast intro from examples/music.md. Preview using ElevenLabs music_v2_5, then save outputs/intro.mp3. Listen for the requested ending and report the measured duration.
```

> Music durations and exact sung lyrics need listening review. A character’s speaking voice does not guarantee the same singer in vocal music. Instrumental and vocal modes cannot be combined.

11 / SOUND EFFECT

## Small sounds with a clear purpose

Specify the event, texture, duration and what should be absent.

Terminal:

```
framechord generate sfx \

  --brief-file examples/sfx.md \
```

sfx.md:


**Ask your agent**

```
Generate a gentle three-second notification sound with FrameChord from examples/sfx.md. Preview first; save to outputs/notification.mp3. Check for unwanted speech, background music and an abrupt ending.
```

<a id="characters"></a>

12 / REUSABLE CHARACTERS

## Define identity once. Review every reuse.

Save stable visual and voice profiles separately from scene direction. Characters are optional for ordinary generation.

![A character reference card connected to three scenes showing the same person in different poses.](media/art-characters.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-characters.yaml)

[![Infographic: Define a character once. 1 Define, 2 Accept, 3 Reuse. Pose, outfit and mood are per-job direction; a new model needs a new character version.](media/info-characters.jpg)](media/info-characters.jpg)

Infographic from an exact spec · Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/info-characters-spec.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord persona add mira
framechord persona show mira --json
framechord templates export authoring
```

Edit the new character’s `persona.md`, `visual.md`, `voice.md` and `character.yaml`. Set explicit models and settings before generation. Templates include identity checklists and reference-sheet briefs.

### Stable identity

Face geometry, eye spacing, hair silhouette, body proportions, materials and distinguishing accessories. The original provider/model and accepted references stay pinned.

### Scene direction

Pose, action, expression, camera and environment belong in the job brief. They must not silently rewrite the character’s canonical identity.

Create candidates, then explicitly accept one:

```
framechord validate --kind character \
  framechord/characters/mira/character.yaml --json

# Paid generation: only run when you want new candidates.
framechord persona bootstrap mira --output-dir candidates --json

# After you select an actual candidate; replace the path below.
framechord persona accept mira --kind image \
  --reference candidates/SELECTED_IMAGE.png
```

> **Acceptance is a separate decision.** Bootstrap does not promote its results. Copy the actual candidate path from its JSON result. Never accept a rejected scene merely to unblock later jobs. The latest Mira/Kito sheets still failed visual review; matching the original model is necessary here but does not guarantee likeness.

### Put two accepted characters in a scene

Terminal:

```
framechord validate --kind job examples/cast.yaml --json
framechord generate --job examples/cast.yaml \
  --output outputs/forest.png --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · cast.yaml, forest.md**

cast.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: forest-play
media: image
brief: forest.md
cast:
  - alias: mira
    character: ../framechord/characters/mira/character.yaml
  - alias: kito
    character: ../framechord/characters/kito/character.yaml
settings:
  format: png
  size: 1536x1024
  image_quality: medium
# Requires both saved characters with accepted references from compatible models.
# These settings assume originals made with OpenAI gpt-image-2.5-flare.
```

forest.md:

```
# A shared forest scene
Mira and Kito play together with fallen leaves in a quiet forest clearing.
Preserve each selected original's face, hair, head/body proportions, materials,
colors and distinguishing accessories. Show both full bodies with ample margins.
Do not blend their identities or change their apparent ages.
```

This example requires your own `mira` and `kito` folders with accepted, compatible original-model references. It intentionally fails validation until those exist.

### Carry a character to another project

Terminal:

```
framechord persona export mira --destination mira-bundle
framechord --project ../another-project persona import mira-bundle
```

Bundles preserve relative dependencies and identity provenance. ID conflicts are rejected. Provider voice bindings remain account-specific.

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Help me define a character with the FrameChord templates. Separate stable identity from scene directions, pin the original provider/model, and show candidates for selection before accepting any reference. For future scenes, compare face and body proportions with the actual accepted originals.
```

<a id="voices"></a>

13 / VOICES

## Reuse a saved voice, or design a candidate

Speech voice identity is independent of visual identity. Start with an accessible provider voice binding.

Terminal:

```
framechord voices --provider elevenlabs --account \
  --page-size 10 --max-pages 1 --json

# Replace YOUR_VOICE_ID with a voice ID accessible to your account.
framechord generate speech --provider elevenlabs \
  --model eleven_v3 --voice YOUR_VOICE_ID \
  --text-file examples/article.txt --format wav \
  --output outputs/saved-voice.wav --dry-run --json
```

For repeatable character speech, save the provider/model, voice binding and delivery description in its voice profile, then use `--character path/to/character.yaml`.

Voice design and creation previews:

```
framechord persona voice-design narrator --model eleven_ttv_v3 \
  --text-file examples/article.txt --run-id narrator-design-1 \
  --dry-run --json

# After generating and selecting an actual design candidate:
framechord persona voice-create narrator \
  --design-run narrator-design-1 --candidate SELECTED_CANDIDATE_ID \
  --name Narrator --bind --dry-run --json
```

First create `narrator` and configure an ElevenLabs speech profile with a voice description. Design returns candidate previews. Creating a saved provider voice and binding it are explicit later operations; remove each preview flag only when intended.

> Recorded cloning uses `persona voice-clone --request clone.yaml`. Start from the bundled clone/consent templates and supply actual selected recordings and permission evidence. Fish recording synthesis uses `--voice-sample`, `--sample-transcript` and `--consent-file`. Do not invent consent or substitute a missing voice.

<a id="agents"></a>

14 / AGENT WORKFLOW

## Use it from any agent with process access

The skill teaches authoring and review. The executable handles credentials, provider requests and local records.

![A terminal at the centre connected to four agent icons, each holding a skill folder.](media/art-agents.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-agents.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord skills install --scope project --agents codex,claude
framechord skills export ./portable-framechord-skill
framechord schema job --json
```

**Skill discovery locations**

| Agent | Project path |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | `.agents/skills/framechord/` (default; also read by Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot) |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/framechord/` (default; also read by Cursor, OpenCode and Copilot) |
| Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot | `--agents cursor,gemini,opencode,copilot` installs `.cursor/skills/`, `.gemini/skills/`, `.opencode/skills/`, `.github/skills/`; `--agents none` installs nothing |
| Other process-based agents | Read the exported `SKILL.md` and references, then call the binary; see [your project](#integrate). |

User-wide installation is a separate choice: `framechord skills install --scope user --agents codex,claude`. It does not change global agent permissions.

**Ask your agent**

Agent prompt:

```
Use the framechord skill. Inspect config and supported models, author YAML and Markdown from the templates, validate locally, and show the resolved request and output destination. Generate only the media I authorize. Use --json --non-interactive, preserve exact scripts, and report artifact paths, failed jobs and uncertain requests accurately.
```

### Let the CLI draft the files

Paid text planning — does not generate media:

```
framechord plan --kind job \
  --provider openai --model gpt-6-luna \
  --prompt "Draft an OpenAI gpt-image-2.5-flare image job for a gardening article cover." \
  --output-dir planned/cover --json --non-interactive
```

> `plan` makes a text-model request and has no `--dry-run` option. Review its returned YAML/Markdown paths, then validate the job before generation. Optional repeated `--character` and `--asset` arguments copy selected dependencies into the planning bundle.

<a id="parallel"></a>

15 / PARALLEL JOBS

## Run independent work together

Keep each job in its own manifest. A batch schedules independent jobs concurrently and preserves successes if another job fails.

![Four conveyor lanes: three parcels arrive with check marks while one waits at a caution marker.](media/art-parallel.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-parallel.yaml)

[![Infographic: Run together, recover safely. Parallel, isolated, cached, and uncertain paid requests are checked rather than resent.](media/info-recovery.jpg)](media/info-recovery.jpg)

Infographic from an exact spec · Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/info-recovery-spec.yaml)

Terminal:

```
framechord validate --kind batch examples/batch.yaml --json
framechord batch --manifest examples/batch.yaml \
  --limits-file examples/limits.yaml \
  --output-dir outputs/batch --dry-run --json
```

**Input files · batch.yaml, image.yaml, speech.yaml, limits.yaml**

batch.yaml:

```
schema_version: 1
jobs:
  - image.yaml
  - speech.yaml
```

image.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-cover
media: image
selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-image-2.5-flare}
brief: image.md
settings: {format: png, size: 1536x1024, image_quality: medium}
```

speech.yaml:

```
schema_version: 2
id: garden-narration
media: speech
selection: {provider: openai, model: gpt-4o-mini-tts}
brief: narration.md
text_file: article.txt
settings: {format: wav, voice: alloy}
locale: en-US
```

limits.yaml:

```
requests: 4
images: 2
audio_seconds: 120
speech_chars: 5000
revisions: 1
attempts: 1
concurrency: 2
per_provider: 2
```

This batch contains one image and one narration. The limits file allows two concurrent jobs, bounded volume and one attempt per job. Limits count requests/media, not dollars. Shared host ceilings still apply.

Terminal:

```
# Paid execution after reviewing the batch preview:
framechord batch --manifest examples/batch.yaml \
  --limits-file examples/limits.yaml --output-dir outputs/batch \
  --async --json --non-interactive

# Replace RUN_ID with the returned run ID.
framechord runs status RUN_ID --json
framechord runs wait RUN_ID
framechord usage --json
```

> Identical effective requests can reuse hash-verified local results. `--fresh` explicitly generates again. `--request-id` provides submission idempotency. Batch failures return nonzero while keeping completed artifacts.

<a id="review"></a>

16 / REVIEW & RECOVERY

## A saved file is the start of review

Generation success means a result was saved and checked structurally. It does not prove accurate text, voice quality or character identity.

![A person comparing two prints on a light table with a magnifier, checklist and headphones.](media/art-review.jpg)

Made with FrameChord · OpenAI `gpt-image-2.5-flare` · [job](media/jobs/art-review.yaml)

Terminal:

```
# Replace ARTIFACT_ID with an ID from generation output.
framechord review check --artifact ARTIFACT_ID --json
framechord review report --artifact ARTIFACT_ID \
  --output comparison.md --json
framechord review status --artifact ARTIFACT_ID --json
```

- **Images:** composition, framing, anatomy and identity against selected originals.
- **Infographics:** every word, value, unit, source note and the reading order.
- **Speech / podcast:** exact script, speaker, pronunciation, missing words and clip joins.
- **Music / effects:** duration, lyrics, texture, distortion and clean endings.

Terminal:

```
# Paid revision: preserves the original and makes a child run.
framechord revise --artifact ARTIFACT_ID \
  --instructions-file examples/revision.md --json
```

**Input files · revision.md**

revision.md:

```
Preserve the original composition and identity. Increase the outer margins so the entire subject is inside the image.
```

For changed copy or scripts, use an updated `--source-job`. A podcast revision can target `--turn guest-answer` and reuse unchanged verified clips. Record an actual assessment with `review record --file review.yaml` and honest human/agent provenance.

Recovery — replace RUN_ID and inspect status first:

```
framechord runs status RUN_ID --json
framechord runs reconcile RUN_ID --json
framechord resume RUN_ID --json
```

> Resume can submit queued or safely retryable work and may incur charges; it preserves successful jobs. Reconciliation can retrieve supported Google interactions with saved request IDs. Other uncertain submissions may need provider/account reconciliation. Do not blindly retry: an unknown request may already have incurred charges. `--retry-unknown` is an explicit paid-risk decision. Local checks and reports make no AI review call; `review check --ai` is a separate paid operation.

- [Every command & flag](#commands): Generated from the bundled CLI help →

This guide targets **FrameChord 0.7.0**. Video generation is outside this version. Provider adapters implement different capabilities; inspect `models --json` before selecting a model. Live model discovery is read-only and does not prove generation readiness.

COMMAND REFERENCE

## Every command. Every flag.

Exact bundled help for all 66 command pages. Expand an entry to inspect its options.

### framechord

```
Generate images, infographics, exact speech, podcasts, music, and sound effects. Use direct flags for one asset or versioned YAML jobs for repeated work. Run --help on any command for inputs, output destinations, and examples. Initialization and validation are offline.

Usage: framechord [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  install    Install this downloaded binary in your user bin directory, offline and without administrator access
  update     Update this executable from a verified public GitHub Release; optional GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN authenticates metadata checks
  init       Initialize offline, preserving existing files and credentials
  config     Inspect or explicitly replace validated configuration
  verify     Preview a bounded live verification suite; execution requires the exact approved preview hash
  usage      Report provider-returned usage separately from unknown costs
  storage    Inspect storage or apply a previously reviewed conservative cleanup plan
  migrate    Preview migration of a v1 job, config or run; --apply creates a non-overwriting backup
  doctor     Inspect credentials offline, or explicitly check all provider endpoints and keys with --live
  notices    Print third-party license notices for components bundled in this binary
  schema     Print a JSON Schema for a versioned manifest
  models     List implemented provider/model capabilities (not account entitlements)
  voices     List built-in voices or search bounded pages of provider account voices
  templates  Inspect or export embedded authoring templates
  persona    Create, inspect, bootstrap, accept, or port character definitions
  validate   Validate local YAML and all referenced files; never generate
  generate   Generate one media job. Example: generate image --prompt 'A forest' --provider openai --model gpt-image-2.5-flare --output forest.png
  batch      Execute independent jobs concurrently using a YAML batch manifest
  runs       Inspect, wait, cancel, or resume durable runs
  resume     Continue a recorded run, preserving successes; ambiguous retries are explicit
  review     Check artifact integrity, request explicit image/audio AI review, or record a human/agent review
  revise     Create a revision child run with inherited identity and limits
  plan       Explicit text-model planning; saves reviewable files without generating media
  skills     Export a portable skill or install it in agent discovery locations
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --project <PROJECT>
          Target project root; credentials are loaded only from this root's .env

          [default: .]

      --json
          Emit a structured JSON result; diagnostics stay on stderr, with no animation

      --non-interactive
          Never prompt; supply YAML files or explicit flags for automation

      --progress <PROGRESS>
          Terminal progress mode; redirected auto progress uses plain stage updates

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, plain, off]

      --color <COLOR>
          Terminal colors; auto honors NO_COLOR

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, always, never]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

```
          Never prompt; supply YAML files or explicit flags for automation
```

```
          [default: .]
```

```
          Audiobook only: generate just these chapter IDs (repeatable); a later run without it assembles the book

      --json
          Emit a structured JSON result; diagnostics stay on stderr, with no animation

      --identity-reference <IDENTITY_REFERENCE>
          Preserve referenced character identities; repeat for multiple selected characters

      --non-interactive
          Never prompt; supply YAML files or explicit flags for automation

      --input-fidelity <INPUT_FIDELITY>
          Historical image-edit fidelity field; omit for current GPT Image 2.5 models

          [possible values: high, low]

      --progress <PROGRESS>
          Terminal progress mode; redirected auto progress uses plain stage updates

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, plain, off]

      --color <COLOR>
          Terminal colors; auto honors NO_COLOR

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, always, never]

      --voice-sample <VOICE_SAMPLE>
          Authorized audio sample for Fish reference synthesis or voice review evidence

      --sample-transcript <SAMPLE_TRANSCRIPT>
          Exact transcript of --voice-sample

      --consent-file <CONSENT_FILE>
          Versioned permission record and referenced evidence for --voice-sample

      --image-quality <IMAGE_QUALITY>
          OpenAI image quality: low/medium/high/auto; current 2.5 models also support xhigh/max

          [possible values: low, medium, high, auto, xhigh, max]

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          [possible values: openai, google, fish, openrouter, elevenlabs]

      --model <MODEL>


      --prompt <PROMPT>
          Creative direction (not speech script); conflicts with --brief-file

      --brief-file <BRIEF_FILE>


      --text <TEXT>
          Exact spoken words; conflicts with --text-file

      --text-file <TEXT_FILE>


      --spec <SPEC>
          Structured infographic YAML

      --character <CHARACTER>
          Character YAML; pins identity, provider/model, and accepted references

      --reference <REFERENCE>


      --voice <VOICE>


      --locale <LOCALE>


      --format <FORMAT>


      --size <SIZE>


      --duration-seconds <DURATION_SECONDS>


      --instrumental


      --vocal
          Request vocal music; conflicts with --instrumental

      --limits-file <LIMITS_FILE>
          Explicit limits YAML for this run (otherwise project limits apply)

      --output <OUTPUT>
          Final filename for a single job; mutually exclusive with --output-dir

      --output-dir <OUTPUT_DIR>
          Directory for final artifacts and podcast clips

      --overwrite
          Explicitly allow replacing a requested destination

      --dry-run
          Validate and print effective inputs without network calls or run creation

      --fresh
          Bypass verified local cache

      --async
          Start a local worker and return the durable run ID

      --request-id <REQUEST_ID>
          Repeated submissions with this ID must have identical effective inputs
```

```
Options:
      --job <JOB>


      --project <PROJECT>
          Target project root; credentials are loaded only from this root's .env

      --file <FILE>


      --json
          Emit a structured JSON result; diagnostics stay on stderr, with no animation

      --format <FORMAT>


      --non-interactive
          Never prompt; supply YAML files or explicit flags for automation

      --fingerprint <FINGERPRINT>


      --progress <PROGRESS>
          Terminal progress mode; redirected auto progress uses plain stage updates

          [possible values: auto, plain, off]

          Terminal colors; auto honors NO_COLOR

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, always, never]

          Markdown reconciliation evidence, without account information or credentials
```
